_comment: The profile for one content type. News, blogs and events are separate
migrations that happen to share code: each has its own folder hierarchy in
Storyblok and its own components, so anything that differs between them
belongs in a file like this rather than in an if-statement in the pipeline.
Copy this file to add a type, change what differs, leave the rest.
label: news story

_comment: Where a story lands. `leaf` is the folder that actually holds the item;
the patterns are chosen by placement, which the taxonomy computes.
Blogs and events can differ here -- a different leaf, or fewer levels.
CONFIRM: where this type lives on aku.edu -- the SOURCE, not the target.
These two are easy to conflate and are not the same thing. `hierarchy.leaf`
is where an item lands in Storyblok. This is where it came from: the path
SharePoint serves it under, the detail page its internal links point at, and
the shape of the id in those links (news_details.aspx?nid=NEWS-1234).
They coincide for news, which is exactly why the /news in build_link_map.py
went unnoticed. For blogs and events the values below are a GUESS -- check a
real internal link in the export before the first run, or every cross-link
will simply fail to resolve and be left pointing at aku.edu.
The component this type becomes, and which bloks its body may contain.
Read off the live space; a type whose schema differs gets its own values
here rather than a fork of build_payload.
How source content maps onto components. Signed off against the
reference story; see docs/PROJECT.md section 5.
spacing is mandatory on every blok -- three values, by component. A blok
without one renders with no vertical rhythm at all.
Source column names. A different SharePoint list may name these
differently; map them here rather than editing the export.
